# FP1: Verstappen leads Russell and Hadjar during first practice at Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

Red Bull's Max Verstappen set the pace during first practice at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Oct 02, 2026 5:50am UTC

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 02:  Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia___Practice/2298168151.webp)

Max Verstappen topped the timesheets during the opening practice hour at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, the Red Bull man setting the pace ahead of George Russell and Isack Hadjar.

With the Sepang International Circuit having last hosted an F1 event back in 2017, many drivers on the grid had not previously experienced the Malaysian track – meaning that Friday’s first practice offered a valuable initial opportunity to get to grips with the venue.

Franco Colapinto led the pack out as the session got underway at 1230 local time, the Alpine racer one of a small number to sport the soft tyres while the majority of the field bolted on the medium compound for their first laps.

Another driver to use the soft rubber was Arvid Lindblad, with the Racing Bulls driver likely to start from the back of the grid on Sunday after the team reported that he would take on a fifth power unit this weekend.

Verstappen – the last driver to win in Malaysia back in 2017 – had gone fastest at the 15-minute mark, while second-placed Russell seemed to be enjoying the challenge of mastering Sepang, the Briton radioing in: “This track is very cool.”

Russell was followed by Kimi Antonelli on the timesheets, with Mercedes running an upgrade for the event as well as sporting a special livery in tribute to their title partner PETRONAS. Meanwhile Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto commented on the high temperatures amid hot and humid conditions.

An even quicker time from Verstappen returned the Dutchman to the top spot on a lap of 1m 37.520s, beating Russell’s effort by nearly four tenths. Antonelli, meanwhile, could go no higher than P5, while a purple first sector for Pierre Gasly helped the Alpine man to slot into seventh.

Elsewhere, the McLaren drivers were each running a different rear wing, with the team hoping for a better weekend after a difficult end to their race last time out in Azerbaijan.

As the session moved into the final quarter, some drivers – including Russell and Antonelli – returned to the medium tyres. The latter looked to be pushing, as replays showed the championship leader having a wide moment out on track.

Amid further laps going on the board in the closing stages – as well as something of a mini race between Esteban Ocon and Carlos Sainz – it was Verstappen who remained on top when the chequered flag fell, followed by Russell and the other Red Bull of Hadjar.

Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were fourth and sixth for Ferrari, separated by Antonelli in fifth, while the top 10 was completed by Gasly, Liam Lawson, Lindblad and the Audi of Nico Hulkenberg.

McLaren’s Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris were 11th and 12th respectively, ahead of Bortoleto, Fernando Alonso in the Aston Martin and the Haas pair of Ocon and Ollie Bearman. Williams’ Alex Albon placed in P17, from Lance Stroll (Aston Martin), Colapinto, Sainz (Williams) and the Cadillacs of Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

# NEED TO KNOW: The most important facts, stats and trivia ahead of the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

As F1 heads to Sepang for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, _Need to Know_ is your all-in-one guide with statistics, driving pointers, strategy tips and more.

Sep 30, 2026 10:55am UTC

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - SEPTEMBER 28:  A general view of the circuit and grandstand during](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/fom-website/2026/Miscellaneous/GettyImages-854947400.webp)

The 2026 Formula 1 season continues this weekend as Sepang hosts Round 16 on the calendar, the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Free Practice 1 and 2 will take place on Friday, October 2, followed by Free Practice 3 and Qualifying on Saturday, October 3, and the Grand Prix itself on Sunday, October 4.

### Vital statistics

- First Grand Prix – 1999 (as the Malaysian Grand Prix)
- Track Length – 5.543km
- Lap record – 1m 34.080s, Sebastian Vettel, Ferrari, 2017
- Most pole positions – Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher (5)
- Most wins – Sebastian Vettel (4)
- Trivia – Sepang was the first F1 track to be designed by renowned circuit architect Hermann Tilke
- Overtakes completed in 2017 – 73
- Safety Car probability – 20%\*
- Virtual Safety Car probability – 20%\*
- Pit stop time loss – 23.7 seconds

\*From the last five Grands Prix at Sepang

![](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9North/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/fom-website/2026/Bahrain%20(Malaysia)/2026trackkualalumpurdetailed.webp)

### The driver’s verdict

Jolyon Palmer, former Renault F1 driver: Sepang is a brilliantly flowing lap, with a fast middle sector splintering big braking zones with plenty of switchback opportunity.

Turn 1 is extremely wide and it’s important to attack the brakes before getting back to hug a late apex to get nicely out of the tighter Turn 2 and up the following curved straight.

The middle sector is all about high-speed balance and flow. A committed entry is needed on the entry for the incredibly high-speed run through 5 before picking your change of direction perfectly into 6 as the track drops away slightly. This is the highest speed cornering section on the circuit. Turn 7 is a bit slower and easy to run wide on the exit before the final part of that sequence which should be an acceleration zone if executed right.

Braking for both Turns 11 and 14 are tricky and all about feel as you are coaxing the car through right hand bends on approach, especially for 14 where it’s easy to lock the right front. Again, the exit of this corner is critical, leading into the final big stamp on the brakes and an overtaking chance at the final turn.

![Lewis Hamilton of Scuderia Ferrari speaks at the media pen during media day of the Formula 1](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/fom-website/2026/Azerbaijan/GettyImages-2296149086.webp)Hamilton has won at the Sepang Circuit on five previous occasions

### Tyre and strategy insight

“Sepang features a relatively abrasive surface, with a level of roughness comparable to Bahrain, while retaining its own distinctive characteristics,” reads Pirelli’s weekend preview. “Grip levels are likely to be low on Friday but should improve progressively over the course of the weekend as the track evolves. One of the main challenges facing teams will be thermal management across both axles.

“The circuit has undergone several changes in recent years. In 2023, the section between Turns 6 and 12 was resurfaced, with further work carried out in the area around Turn 9. However, the overall characteristics of the surface, as assessed by Pirelli engineers just a few weeks ago, remain very similar to those recorded in 2017.

“More recently, from the beginning of September, additional surface levelling work was carried out to remove irregularities in the asphalt, alongside cleaning operations aimed at improving track conditions ahead of the World Championship event.

“Teams will also have to contend with a lack of available data. Despite being a historic venue, no team possesses truly relevant references relating to the current generation of Formula 1 cars.

"As a result, Friday practice sessions will be more important than usual, both for drivers, who will need to familiarise themselves with a circuit that many have only experienced in the simulator, and for teams, which must identify the correct car balance and assess tyre behaviour.

“While there is no shortage of technical unknowns, the weather could add a further layer of complexity. Afternoon thunderstorms are a regular feature of the region in early October and could affect any session during the weekend. Intense heat, high humidity and sudden downpours have always been among the defining characteristics of the Malaysian Grand Prix during its years as a permanent fixture on the Formula 1 calendar.”

![](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/fom-website/2026/Bahrain%20(Malaysia)/16-bh26-preview-en.webp)

### Current Form

[Kimi Antonelli](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/kimi-antonelli) remains at the top of the [drivers' standings](https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2026/drivers) despite a sub-optimal weekend in Baku, where a crash in Qualifying meant the [Mercedes](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/mercedes) did well to salvage fifth in the race.

In contrast, team mate [George Russell](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/george-russell) enjoyed possibly his best weekend of the season, taking a dominant pole before holding off [Max Verstappen](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/max-verstappen) in the closing stages for his third victory of the year, bringing Antonelli's margin down to 66 points.

Verstappen was just one tenth off his first win of the season, but [Red Bull](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/red-bull-racing) look to be finding form as [Isack Hadjar](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/isack-hadjar) claimed a podium on his return from a wrist injury.

Azerbaijan proved to be a disaster for [McLaren](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/mclaren) as neither driver scored, with reigning World Champion [Lando Norris](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/lando-norris) eliminated in a crash, but the Briton has previously proven to be the closest challenger to Mercedes prior to the last round.

[Ferrari](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/ferrari), meanwhile, left Baku with a double points finish and will be looking to find greater performance to once again challenge for wins.

In the midfield fight, [Racing Bulls](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/racing-bulls) pulled further ahead of [Alpine](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/alpine) in the [teams' standings](https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2026/team) as they battle for P5, with [Franco Colapinto](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/franco-colapinto) set to serve a five-place grid penalty in Sepang for the Baku incident that eliminated himself and team mate [Pierre Gasly](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/pierre-gasly).

[Haas](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/haas) will be looking to score more points after the team's first double points finish, while [Williams](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/williams)' major upgrade gave [Carlos Sainz](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/carlos-sainz) the chance to finish inside the top 10 for the first time since May.

# FP3: Antonelli goes fastest from Verstappen and Hadjar during final practice at Bahrain GP in Malaysia

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli set the pace for the first time during the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia weekend by going quickest in Free Practice 3.

Oct 03, 2026 5:48am UTC

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 02: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9South/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia___Practice/2298211592.webp)

Kimi Antonelli ended the third and final practice session at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on top of the timesheets, the Mercedes driver setting the pace ahead of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

After what the Silver Arrows described as one of their “toughest Fridays of the season”, the team looked to have enjoyed a much stronger start to Saturday as Antonelli worked his way down to a 1m 36.302s, putting him nearly three tenths clear of Verstappen.

It was a relatively quiet start to the session when the green light appeared at 1230 local time, with Cadillac’s Sergio Perez – one of 10 current drivers present on the grid when Formula 1 last raced at Sepang in 2017 – being the first to hit the track.

More cars started to emerge as the clock ticked down, many sporting the soft tyres for their opening runs on another day of hot and humid conditions, and Charles Leclerc – bucking the trend by using the hard compound – set an early benchmark by recording a lap of 1m 37.772.

The McLaren pair emerged on the medium tyres, with Lando Norris promptly displacing Leclerc at the top of the timesheets by going six tenths faster. Team mate Oscar Piastri slotted into second, albeit three tenths away from Norris’ time.

A red flag was thrown just before the halfway point of the session due to some debris on track, with replays showing that this had come from Ollie Bearman’s Haas. Some drivers were yet to make an appearance by this stage, including the Mercedes pair, Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

Practice 3 results

[View all standings](https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2026/races/1308/bahrain/practice/3)

That all changed when the action resumed as a queue of cars emerged from the pit lane. Red Bull joined McLaren in opting for the medium tyres, while most remained on the soft rubber – including Antonelli, who went quickest on a 1m 36.924s.

Verstappen, meanwhile, set the fastest first sector but wound up in fourth place, the Dutchman having seemingly encountered traffic later on in his lap. Others also seemed to be facing this issue on an increasingly busy track, with Hamilton seen waving his hand after finding himself stuck behind the slower-moving Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad.

With 15 minutes left on the clock, the McLaren pair switched to the soft tyres – but Norris’ effort was not enough to lift him higher than his P3 slot, while Piastri also remained in fifth place. Aston Martin, meanwhile, caught the eye as Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll moved up to 11th and 14th respectively.

Most of the field were back on the circuit as the session neared its end, and Leclerc improved to split the Mercedes cars in second place. The order rapidly evolved, however, as others crossed the line, with Antonelli going even quicker at the top while Verstappen and Hadjar slotted into second and third.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 03: Oliver Bearman of Great Britain driving the (87) Haas F1 VF-26](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9South/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia___Qualifying/2298329804.webp)A red flag was briefly thrown when a small piece of debris came off Bearman's Haas

Antonelli’s impressive lap of 1m 36.302s kept him in P1 as the hour drew to a close, Verstappen being 0.278s adrift in P2 while Hadjar was half a second back in third. George Russell had a six-tenths deficit to his team mate in P4, and the Ferrari duo of Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton followed in fifth and sixth.

Norris and Piastri were seventh and eighth, with Franco Colapinto in the Alpine and Lindblad rounding out the top 10. Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto just missed out in P11, ahead of Alonso, Pierre Gasly (Alpine), Esteban Ocon (Haas), Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) and Nico Hulkenberg (Audi).

Bearman placed in 17th, followed by Carlos Sainz (Williams), Stroll, Alex Albon (Williams), Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) and Perez.

With the final practice hour complete, the attentions of the paddock will now switch to Qualifying, which is set to get underway at 1600 local time.

# Winners and Losers - Malaysia

Oct 02, 2017 12:00am UTC

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcd1701oc520.webp)

You learn to expect the unexpected in Formula 1, and at Sepang this weekend the formbook was all over the place. So whose final Malaysian Grand Prix was a hit, and who won't be missing the race come next year?

### The Winners

### Victorious Verstappen

He said on Saturday that he really wanted to win a race the hard way, rather than having it gifted to him as he thought had been the case in Spain last year. And in the end, Max Verstappen was granted his wish the day after his 20th birthday.

It was richly deserved.

The Dutch star has had a pretty dispiriting year, with seven DNFs and his last podium appearance in China back in April. A year to forget, he called it.

But things started to go his way when Sebastian Vettel hit trouble in qualifying and went to the back of the grid, and continued when front-row qualifier Kimi Raikkonen’s Ferrari encountered similar turbo pressure problems on its grid lap, and was eventually pushed to its garage, from whence it never reappeared.

After taking second place behind Lewis Hamilton at the start, Verstappen trailed the struggling Mercedes for three more laps before slicing aggressively down the inside into Turn 1. He knew Hamilton could not afford to defend too seriously, given the world championship points situation, and once that mighty job was done he controlled the race, and himself, to score an excellent and much-needed victory.

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcc1701oc871.webp)

### Rejuvenated Red Bull

As if Verstappen winning at last wasn’t big enough headline news for Red Bull, the Milton Keynes team also had Daniel Ricciardo’s third place to celebrate.

But it wasn’t just the strong 1-3 result and the relief that the Dutchman would be happy again after all his recent misfortunes. It was the fact that the RB13 was good enough in Sepang to get its own back on Mercedes after their surprise superior performance in Singapore last time out.

The indications are that, since Adrian Newey turned his attention back to the aerodynamics of the car, Red Bull have turned a corner. They looked good at Monza and Singapore, besides of course Hungary, and they think they will be pretty good for the rest of the season.

That’s great news for F1, if it means a third team getting into the mix. Less so for Ferrari and Mercedes, who could lose valuable points if they have a tough weekend.

![_ONY5338.jpg](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/manual/Homepage%20Carousel/2017/_ONY5338.webp)

### Lady luck with Lewis and Mercedes

Strictly speaking, this duo lost, as their run of three wins was halted. Yet they didn’t. They turned things around dramatically after what Toto Wolff called their “worst ever” Friday, switching the Briton back to a Singapore specification aerodynamic set-up. And Hamilton won again when, finding himself in two minds after team mate Valtteri Bottas went quite well too in FP3 while retaining the new configuration which hadn’t worked on Friday, he was unable to revert to it because of the complexity involved.

Come the race, that was a blessing as team mate Bottas struggled, and a strong second place was perfect damage limitation on a day when the F1 W08 lacked the sheer pace to run with Max Verstappen’s Red Bull.

As a result, Hamilton increased his championship lead over Sebastian Vettel to 34 points with five races remaining.

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcd1701oc1191.webp)

### Plucky Perez

Sergio Perez drove a heroic race to sixth for Force India, considering that he had been laid low with such a nasty virus that the team had him on an intravenous drip for the previous two nights. He went into the race feeling awful, and looked utterly washed out by the finish of the most physically arduous Grand Prix on the calendar, yet he made a brilliant start and didn’t put a wheel wrong the whole way.

“That,” he said with feeling, “was the toughest race I have ever driven.” His bright pink VJM10 certainly had better colour, as his face was sheet-white.

“I feared I would need to give up,” he confessed. But he didn’t. “It’s an amazing result just to make it to the finish: I just kept going out of willingness to do it and I have to thank the doctors for helping me out.

“Having a good start was the key to my race and so was passing Vandoorne during the first few laps. After that, I was able to manage my race and it was all pretty uneventful. We were able to extend the first stint and manage our tyres well. I was only under pressure from Vettel, but that was not really my fight.

“We scored some more important points for the team and I am happy to come home with a good result after such a difficult weekend.”

Truly, this was one of the drives of the race.

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcd1701oc925.webp)

### Vandoorne’s demon drive

A very strong race from Stoffel Vandoorne brought McLaren seventh place on a day when Fernando Alonso could not finish better than 11th, and the Belgian had out-qualified the Spaniard, too.

"I’m very, very happy today, this definitely was my best drive in Formula 1 up until now," the Belgian said. "To finish seventh here, and to qualify seventh as well - just an extremely solid race. I had to push every lap, take care of the tyres, and bring the car home. They were tough conditions out there, but we managed the gap with Lance \[Stroll\] very well, so I’m extremely happy.

"The last races have been very, very good as well for me. I'm definitely working hard with the team, putting the pressure on, and it's good for the team spirit. This weekend shows that when everything falls more or less together, when we extract the most out of the car, great things are possible. And lately, even when things don't go 100 percent right, I'm still able to recover much better. All the effort I've been putting in is paying off massively."

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcc1701oc702.webp)

### Pascal proves his worth

Pascal Wehrlein finished only 17th in his uncompetitive Sauber, but in its own way that was a victory because the German, with no guarantee of an F1 seat for 2018, set a very respectable 10th fastest lap. He had started on the soft Pirelli tyres and did not stop for the supersofts until the 37th lap, but it wasn’t a case of a set of fresh tyres allowing him to do better than his fellow drivers. That quick lap came on the 53rd of 56, so that was a pretty impressive effort. Oh, and then he gave Vettel a lift back to the pits.

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcd1701oc520.webp)

### The Losers

### Calamity for Kimi

Poor Kimi Raikkonen. In both Monaco and Hungary he was quick enough to win, but the team situation denied him the chance, With Vettel on the back row here, he was positively encouraged to go out and get the job done.

Instead, as he drove to the grid he felt a loss of power similar to that which Vettel had encountered in qualifying.

The team eventually had to wheel his SF70H off the grid for attention in the Ferrari garage, from which it never emerged.

Based on the speed that Vettel was able to demonstrate in his climb through the field, victory had been there for the taking for the Finn.

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcc1701oc172.webp)

### Valiant Vettel

In many ways Vettel was a winner, because of the mature way in which he handled his disappointment in FP3 and qualifying, and the sheer tiger he showed as he came storming through the field thanks to a string of fastest laps.

Perhaps he was not robust enough in attacking Daniel Ricciardo in Turn 1 on the 49th lap. Equally though, his championship position, like Hamilton’s, precluded such heroics.

Ultimately, he could no longer sustain his challenge and fell back, then had that needless incident with Lance Stroll as both chose the same piece of track to gather rubber on the slow-down lap. If he needs a gearbox change for Suzuka as a result, that will mean a costly grid penalty.

He left Malaysia 34 points down on Hamilton, and now needs a fair bit of luck to pull off a fifth title, the speed of the SF70H notwithstanding.

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcc1701oc238.webp)

### Bold Bottas in Mercedes mire

Valtteri Bottas admits that he is at the most difficult stage of his career after string of less than stellar performances followed his impressive early-season drives.

It didn’t help him that he had the new aerodynamic configuration that didn’t work in Sepang, but there is blame on his side too.

“Today was difficult,” he confessed after the race. “I was trying everything I could, I was giving it all I had, but I was lacking pace and I was sliding around. The start was definitely the best part of the day. It was really good, I could actually attack a little bit and fight for positions.”

He almost got round the outside of Verstappen for second at one stage.

“But not long after that I just started to drop down and couldn't keep up with the others. In the first stint I had quite a lot of understeer, so I was struggling with the balance. The story of the race was managing the tyre temperatures. If I tried harder, then I started to overheat the tyre and slide even more, so I had to manage everything and that's why I was so slow.

“We need to analyse the race because the upgrade package should have been quite a step forward in terms of downforce, but I couldn't really see it. There are still a lot of things we need to try to understand, we need to learn from today. For Japan, we need to make sure we choose all the right bits for the car, and hopefully we will see some cooler temperatures.”

There is support for him at Mercedes, however.

In the words of team boss Toto Wolff: “A wise man once said that smooth seas do not tough sailors make.”

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcd1701oc776.webp)

### Ocon in the wars

Ocon was unlucky at the start. Force India team mate Sergio Perez made a superb one, and when the two arrived at Turn 2, Ocon found the Mexican on the inside to the left off him, and Felipe Massa’s Williams to his right. He was thus the meat in the sandwich. He sustained a puncture in the resultant clash with Massa, and thus had to pit on the third lap.

That consigned him to run for 53 laps on a set of soft Pirellis, during which time he also clashed with Sainz, his right rear to the Spaniard’s front left, in Turn 1 on the 25th lap. That spun him down from ninth to 12th, and meant that he could only to recover to 10th on a day when he could have been sixth or seventh.

“It’s a race to forget for me because the pace of the car was strong and we couldn’t maximise it,” he said.

![Formula One World](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2017/Malaysia/Sunday/dcc1701oc740.webp)

# Who gained and lost the most places on a chaotic first racing lap in Sepang?

It was a dramatic start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with drivers splitting their tyre choices amid mixed weather conditions.

Oct 04, 2026 11:52am UTC

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9South/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298494507.webp)

F1 fans were treated to a show during the first lap of racing action at the Sepang International Circuit on Sunday, thanks to pre-race rain, a rapidly drying track surface and a host of different tyre selections.

The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was initially delayed due to thunderstorms in the area, and the first race start procedure then got suspended when several drivers struggled to maintain speed on the formation lap.

After a lengthy wait, the race eventually began in slippery, mixed conditions, which led to split tyre strategies and plenty of early movement up and down the order.

While a portion of drivers opted for intermediate tyres, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Pierre Gasly, Gabriel Bortoleto, Nico Hulkenberg, Ollie Bearman, Valtteri Bottas, Sergio Perez and Franco Colapinto all chose soft slicks, and Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll bolted on mediums.

Struggling for grip, Perez pitted at the end of the first lap behind the Safety Car to take on intermediates, with Piastri, Bortoleto, Stroll and Hulkenberg following suit a lap later – meaning they lined up in the pit lane as their rivals tackled a standing start.

# What the teams said – Friday in Malaysia
### Red Bull
[Max Verstappen](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/max-verstappen) topped the opening session for [Red Bull](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/red-bull-racing) by a comfortable margin, and with [Isack Hadjar](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/isack-hadjar) in P3, the car looked strong out of the box. In the second session, Hadjar impressed again with p2, while Verstappen was fourth, but crucially was the only driver not to run the soft tyre, thus setting his lap time on the mediums.

Max Verstappen - FP1: 1:37.520, P1; FP2: 1:37.785, P4

“I think we had a pretty decent start today. We began well; the track was quite tricky as it was very hot with a lot of degradation, so there are a few things, particularly with the tyres, that we will need to analyse tonight.

# What the teams said – Friday in Malaysia

The drivers and teams report back on all the action from Friday practice for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit.

Oct 02, 2026 12:04pm UTC (20 hours ago)![](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/content/dam/fom-website/2018-redesign-assets/Author/Becky_Hart.png)Special ContributorBecky Hart

### Red Bull

[Max Verstappen](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/max-verstappen) topped the opening session for [Red Bull](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/red-bull-racing) by a comfortable margin, and with [Isack Hadjar](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/isack-hadjar) in P3, the car looked strong out of the box. There were some question marks about overheating, but the same could be said for most of the field. In the second session, Hadjar impressed again with p2, while Verstappen was fourth, but crucially was the only driver not to run the soft tyre, thus setting his lap time on the mediums.

The bad news for Hadjar is it has been confirmed he will take a five-place grid drop for Sunday’s race for fitting a new ICE.

Max Verstappen - FP1: 1:37.520, P1; FP2: 1:37.785, P4

“I think we had a pretty decent start today. We began well; the track was quite tricky as it was very hot with a lot of degradation, so there are a few things, particularly with the tyres, that we will need to analyse tonight. It was warmer in FP2 and a different programme that we were running, so it is quite difficult to compare the progress between the two sessions. There are still a few things we need to understand better ahead of tomorrow, but we have had two positive sessions, which is good.”

Isack Hadjar - FP1: 1:38.303, P3; FP2: 1:37.627, P2

“A very good start to the weekend in terms of competitiveness. The track is very challenging and the conditions are tough, so I feel there's still a lot of lap time to find. I'm not completely happy with the balance of the car yet, but I'm super happy with our overall competitiveness. Tomorrow, I think Qualifying is going to be very short and sharp, with only a few laps available on the tyres, but I'm looking forward to it. I think we have a good car this weekend and that we can fight at the front.”

Pierre Wache, Technical Director

“It’s been a challenging day here at Sepang, but also a very interesting one. It has been quite demanding for the drivers and the car because of the heat, but I think we have made a good start to the weekend.

"The track surface was extremely dusty, and the grip evolved a lot throughout the day, but we made a good start in the opening session, evaluating the package we brought to Baku and focusing on different types of corners, particularly in the low speed. Overall, it seems to be working better than what we brought last weekend.

"In the second session, we had expected rain but, when that didn’t appear, we prioritised the long run on the Medium tyre, as gaining data on tyre behaviour and degradation will be the most important thing for the rest of the weekend. In the end, that meant we ran out of time for Max to run the Soft, but Isack had the opportunity, and that was valuable. Isack had a few issues in the session with balance, but we will do our best to iron those out overnight. After that, in terms of relative performance, it is very difficult to judge, but so far, we are happy with where we are.”

Roll on the second session, and [Charles Leclerc](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/charles-leclerc) wound up on top of the timing sheets with an impressive flying lap on the softs. ### Mercedes

[George Russell](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/george-russell) started his weekend in Malaysia well, looking strong in the opening session. He finished second behind Verstappen, but while his one-lap pace was quick, Russell was concerned about tyre wear in his [Mercedes](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/mercedes). As for [Kimi Antonelli](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/kimi-antonelli), he was a little bit off the pace as his weekend began in slightly more circumspect fashion. Both made a mistake through the final corner on their one flying lap on the softs in FP2, and thus did not set fully representative lap times. But if they can nail that tricky final corner, they look right in the mix here.

Kimi Antonelli - FP1: 1:38.580, P5; FP2: 1:38.060, P8

"We have had a decent first day on track here in Malaysia. The PETRONAS Sepang International Circuit is incredible to drive! It is fast and flowing so it’s super cool. We were able to complete lots of running across both sessions and worked through a full programme too. We gathered plenty of data, both useful for understanding the new update we’ve brought here and for helping us make improvements over the rest of the weekend here in Malaysia.

"We’ve still got a lot of work to do though. The Red Bulls look the fastest on both the single lap and the long run, with McLaren and Ferrari also competitive on higher fuel in particular. The track was quite low grip today and it is likely that it will improve into Saturday and Sunday. We will work hard tonight to find improvements overnight and do our best come qualifying tomorrow afternoon."

George Russell - FP1: 1:37.903, P2; FP2: 1:38.020, P7

"It was a really cool experience to get out on track for the first time here at the PETRONAS Sepang International Circuit. I’ve never driven here before and it’s great to do so given how iconic this place is. The support we’ve had here as a team is also amazing so thanks for all the fans for coming out today and over the weekend.

"With these warm conditions, combined with the aggressive tarmac and the characteristics of the circuit, the tyre degradation throughout practice was high. That was as we expected coming into the weekend but with the amount of overheating on the tyres, it slightly neutralises the performance of any extra downforce we’ve added with our update. The cars are operating in quite a different window to what we usually do, and I don’t think we quite got ours into the place that we needed today. We will look to get on top of that overnight and hopefully, if we do so, we can be in the fight at the front for the rest of the weekend."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"We were running the latest update package on both cars today but rather than seeing the step in lap time that we had hoped for, we have been chasing a tricky balance and a fair amount of tyre overheating. We had a few test items on the cars in FP1 that might have clouded the situation but for FP2, we had both cars in a representative configuration, and it looked like we were still trailing, especially to the Red Bull.

"We've got some good ideas for setup changes to investigate during the overnight simulator work and will continue to analyse today's data to understand why we seem to lack a bit of a pace. we're optimistic that with such a new package, these analyses will bear some fruit. The headline times are not especially representative, and we should be able to make some relatively easy progress on the single lap pace. Our concern is more the long run where we seemed unusually offset on pace and that is going to be the more challenging problem to solve."

[McLaren](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/mclaren) did not look to be chasing outright pace in FP1, instead using the session to test out different rear wing configurations on each car. Whatever they discovered, their drivers were evenly matched with just 0.017s between them.
They did run a more conventional programme in FP2, with [Lando Norris](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/lando-norris) impressing on his flying lap to grab third, just over a tenth off the pace. [Oscar Piastri](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/oscar-piastri) was a few places further back, but it certainly looks like McLaren [have the speed to compete for pole](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/mclaren-explain-what-caught-us-by-surprise-in-malaysia-as-piastri-reflects-on-where-they-stack-up.sDpGuLb4lFAQWOfgApwQR) tomorrow, especially if they can dial in their set-up that tiny bit more.

Lando Norris - FP1: 1:39.293, P12; FP2: 1:37.665, P3

"An interesting first day here at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. Nice to get our first laps in around this circuit, it's a fun track and an interesting challenge in terms of layout and track surface. We're struggling more than we'd like to, but we made some progress going into FP2. We've still got quite a bit more to solve if we want to be competitive, but we'll look at the data this evening and see what we can do going into FP3 and Qualifying tomorrow."

Oscar Piastri - FP1: 1:39.276, P11; FP2: 1:37.899, P6

“That’s Friday at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia done. It was a reasonable day for us. From FP1 into FP2, we made a solid amount of progress, which meant we finished the day well. Our Quali sims and longer runs felt pretty good. But we still have a lot to find overnight and a lot more to understand about racing here. The true long-run performance across the grid, including for us, is still a bit of an unknown for everyone, but it feels like we could be in the mix.

“The circuit is a cool one to drive, but we’re finding the grip and high tyre degradation are really challenging. We need to understand both better overnight to put us in a better position ahead of Qualifying. Our goal is to build on today’s positive momentum and extract as much performance as possible to ensure we’re competitive.”

Randy Singh, Senior Director, Racing

“We found the track conditions quite surprising today. It was a lot rougher and had more grip than our initial forecasts suggested. This presented a challenge in FP1, where we struggled to get the car into an optimal window. However, the team did a fantastic job, both here at the circuit and back at the factory, to analyse the data and dial the car in much better for the second session. We felt far more comfortable in FP2 and made a solid step forward.

“Tyre degradation was the main talking point, and it was consistently high all day, which will definitely be a major factor in the race. The hot, abrasive surface is really tough on the tyres. From a strategy perspective, the high degradation naturally pushes things towards a two-stop, as the numbers make a three-stop very difficult without other factors like a Safety Car. We still have plenty of work ahead of us to fine-tune everything for Qualifying, but we are focused on exploiting the full potential of our package.”

So, it makes a lot of sense to get in the best possible shape for the race, as we know that even if we were to make it to Q3, we will be towards the back anyway. We tried a lot of things and different set-ups and the pace looked relatively competitive and comparable to others. We knew at some point we would have to take a penalty for power unit components, like some of our rivals, and we felt this track might be optimal for overtaking and allows more of an opportunity for Franco to work his way through the field, like we saw him do in Monza on his way to the points. "It's been a fairly positive day here at the Bahrain GP. The track is fun to drive but very hard on tyres, particularly given the fact it hasn't been resurfaced in a few years. It's also extremely hot here in Malaysia, which is physically tough. However, our training and preparation should put us in a strong position ahead of Qualifying tomorrow, where tyre management will be key."

Alan Permane, Team Principal

"First of all, it’s good to be back in Malaysia, Kuala Lumpur is a great city and the circuit will produce an exciting weekend, I’m sure. It’s been a positive day for us today, we’re happy with the performance of both cars and feel we made a step up in between the sessions. The track is a lot smoother than we anticipated, so we made some set-up changes ahead of FP2 to make the most of those conditions. Arvid’s engine change was something we knew we would need to do in the next few races, and we felt this was the most strategic place to do it. With the tyre deg being quite high, there's certainly some overtaking possibilities to be had, so we feel like we've made the right decision. It will certainly be a challenge for him to fight his way through the pack and into the points from the back, but it’s not impossible.”

### Audi

Both [Audi](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/audi) drivers had moments in FP1, straddling the kerbs and getting it all a bit wrong. But as the grip improved, they were able to extract lap time and [Nico Hulkenberg](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/nico-hulkenberg) even finished the session in the top 10. The German fell back slightly in FP2, while [Gabriel Bortoleto](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/gabriel-bortoleto) had a couple more moments. First much to his frustration, the Brazilian had to abort a flying run after coming up behind Hamilton who was on the racing line. Then he got on the kerbs after trying a move on Lindblad, before following his rival through a number of corners as he eventually lined up an overtake through Turn 3.

But Bortoleto stopped out on track late on with an apparent gearbox issue, not the ideal way for his Friday to end.

Nico Hulkenberg - FP1: 1:39.211, P10; FP2: 1:39.109, P13

"Coming back to Sepang after so many years meant there was plenty to learn again, and the heat definitely added another challenge. We worked through the programme and gathered a lot of information, but there are still a few areas we need to understand a bit better. We'll go through everything overnight and see where we can find a bit more grip and balance."

Gabriel Bortoleto - FP1: 1:39.548, P13; FP2: 1:39.051, P12

“It was an interesting day, and thankfully the issue we had at the end of FP2 didn’t cost us time. We had a few items to test going from FP1 to FP2, and, overall, we can be quite satisfied with our work. There are still some areas where we can improve, so we’ll work through the data tonight and try to make a few steps forward for tomorrow. But overall, it was a good day and a positive start to the weekend.”

### Haas

[Esteban Ocon](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/esteban-ocon) pipped his team mate in the opening session but had one hairy moment fighting with Sainz towards the end of the session. The Frenchman attempted to overtake, but ran wide over the kerbs as he got on the dusty part of the track, just managing to avoid the grass. He was again the quicker of the two [Haas](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/haas) drivers in FP2, seemingly having the edge on [Ollie Bearman](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/oliver-bearman) here. But Haas need to find a few tenths if they want to battle towards the front of the midfield.

Esteban Ocon – FP1: 1:40.158, P15; FP2: 1:39.361, P14

“It was a positive day. First of all, it’s an amazing track to drive again. I remembered it back then as awesome, but driving it again is pure joy every lap. I had fun today, it’s been positive, and we improved the car from FP1 to FP2. Although we still have work to do tonight, we look healthy on the car-side, and it’s performing as it should, so it’s been positive and we need to keep going like that.”

Oliver Bearman - FP1: 1:40.311, P16; FP2: 1:39.706, P16

“It’s been a tough day for us, to be honest. We looked a bit less competitive than what we were probably expecting on low-fuel. On high-fuel, it looks a bit better, but in general, it’s been a tough day for us. On my side, I’ve been learning the track as well and I feel like I’ve made progress, but in FP2, I felt a bit of a lack in confidence, which adds up to a lot of lap time around here. I’m confident we can do a better job tomorrow.”

Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal

“It was a bit of a tricky Friday. On Esteban’s side of the garage it was pretty clean, he did a good job. Of course, we’ve got things to improve but it was a clean pair of sessions. The same cannot be said on Ollie’s side of the garage, where I think we’ve still got this issue with parts, where putting a certain part or a different part doesn’t necessarily behave exactly the same. We had very different feedback across the garage in FP1, and Ollie was much happier in FP1 compared to FP2, and that wasn’t down to track conditions. We really have to dive into this one – we have some ideas, but tonight we need to solve it, because we could then get to the limit of this package and fight in Q2. If we don’t do that, we’ll be out in Q1, so it’s critical that we find out what’s going on with Ollie’s car.”

### Aston Martin

[Fernando Alonso](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/fernando-alonso) is one of three drivers in the field who knows what it takes to win here, having done so three times previously. He started well in the opening session with a P14 finish, and was only one place lower in the second session. That bodes well after a tricky time of it in Baku, but the Spaniard did lock-up at one point, with conditions still testing everyone. In the other [Aston Martin](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/aston-martin), [Lance Stroll](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/lance-stroll) was a few places further back, so might want to analyse his team mate’s data tonight to see where he can find some time.

Fernando Alonso - FP1: 1:39.683, P14; FP2: 1:39.478, P15

Lance Stroll - FP1: 1:40.413, P18; FP2: 1:40.150, P18

Fernando Alonso said:

"We haven't had time to analyse anything in depth as we have just got out of the car.

"We do need to work on finding more grip and optimising the setup of the car for the rest of the weekend. There is a lot of tyre degradation with extreme temperatures and a rough tarmac."

Pedro de la Rosa, Team Ambassador said:

"Coming back to Malaysia after such a long time, there were many unknowns, but we got two decent sessions in today and managed to complete our Friday programme.

"Sepang is obviously a very different track to last weekend and we came here expecting the track characteristics to suit our package a bit more than Baku so hopefully we can show some more competitiveness here.

"Nevertheless, it’s only Friday and we still have work to do, especially with the car balance on Lance’s side.

"Fernando seemed okay with the car balance today. He mainly reported issues with low grip of the tarmac but that’s the same issue for everyone else so we just have to adapt to that. But it will be challenging for the drivers and it also means it’s easy to make mistakes."

### Williams

[Williams](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/williams) are still assessing their upgrade package that went onto the car in Baku. As such, FP1 was about data gathering, with both [Alex Albon](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/alexander-albon) and [Carlos Sainz](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/carlos-sainz) winding up a little down the order. They remained off the pace in FP2, but it remains to be seen whether they were running a different programme and not chasing pure performance yet. One thing was for sure, Albon was not happy with the set-up of his car, complaining about his deployment and rear stability amongst other things.

Alex Albon - FP1: 1:40.321, P17; FP2: 1:40.221, P20

“This is such a unique track and it's really physical to drive. The car doesn't feel great yet, so we've got a lot of work to do overnight. We made some changes ahead of FP2 to improve our low speed, but we lost a bit of the medium and high speed, which had actually felt better than expected. Hopefully we get some rain or something unpredictable this weekend that we can take advantage of."

Carlos Sainz - FP1: 1:40.605, P20; FP2: 1:39.930, P17

“Very difficult Friday for us. Unfortunately, we see that on this track we are back to performing at the level that we were, towards the end of the grid, unless we find something extraordinary going into the weekend. We did some setup changes that helped in FP2, but we continue to struggle at high speed, long corners which also affects our degradation on such a rough tarmac. We’ll keep working on solutions for tomorrow and Sunday."

Paul Williams - Chief Engineer, Trackside Performance

“Coming into this weekend, we knew it was going to be a challenge and was going to stetch the capabilities of the upgraded package, but we’ve had two clean sessions to gather data and we’re already finding some useful data points for us to dig into further. We knew that Baku was a stronger circuit for us, so it’s important that we can test out the package and the known limitations of the car around a circuit that exposes these weaknesses, ensuring we’re isolating these characteristics and not carrying them into next year.

"The high tyre degradation from the rough track surface and high track temperature will dominate the race. It is also important to achieve a balance front and rear tyre preparation on low fuel. We’ll review the data tonight to prepare heading into FP3 and qualifying tomorrow."

### Pirelli

Simone Berra, Pirelli Chief Engineer

"Track conditions played a decisive role in tyre behaviour throughout this opening day at Sepang. From the outset, grip levels were low due to dust on the surface and a particularly abrasive track that requires a significant amount of rubbering-in before it can deliver its full potential.

"This had a clear impact on track evolution and lap times, to the extent that Friday’s fastest lap remained virtually unchanged between FP1 and FP2. The benchmark time was more than four seconds slower than the qualifying simulation reference, a mark that the cars may struggle to approach tomorrow.

"The sessions were also characterised by high thermal degradation, generated by tyre sliding and the nature of the track surface, with a significant impact particularly during the long runs.

"The absence of the forecast rain during FP2 allowed teams to complete a number of race simulations, enabling us to gather substantial data on the C3 and C4 compounds, which displayed very similar levels of performance in terms of both pace and degradation.

"At times, the Soft proved more consistent than the Medium because its higher level of grip helps limit sliding and, consequently, heat generation. The performance delta between the two compounds is around half a second, in line with expectations. The Hard remains an unknown quantity, however, as teams chose not to use it and instead preserve their available sets for the race.

"With degradation levels similar to those seen today, performance drop-off is between two and three tenths of a second per lap. As a result, Sunday’s race could be shaped by two or more pit stops, which was precisely the outcome we hoped to encourage through the compound selection for this event. Before defining a more precise scenario, however, it will be necessary to carry out a further analysis of the data collected throughout the day."

# HIGHLIGHTS: Watch the action from a tense Hungarian GP as Verstappen and Red Bull make history

Jul 23, 2023 3:57pm UTC

Max Verstappen took a dominant seventh consecutive win of the season at this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix, with the Dutch driver leading home the McLaren of Lando Norris and Red Bull team mate Sergio Perez.

Starting from second on the grid, Verstappen made a brilliant getaway to take the lead at Turn 1, setting him up for a commanding ninth win of the year. Pole-sitter Lewis Hamilton lost out in the early exchanges dropping down to fourth, which is where he would finish.

[READ MORE: Verstappen dominates Hungarian GP to give Red Bull a record 12th successive win](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.verstappen-dominates-hungarian-gp-to-give-red-bull-a-record-12th-successive.Y7z82iKtBfCKYRnYNUQsU.html)

Norris was able to hold off the fast charging Perez – who recovered from starting ninth on the grid to finish third – with the Briton taking his second consecutive P2 finish.

The other McLaren of Oscar Piastri followed Hamilton home in fifth, with George Russell benefitting from Charles Leclerc's five-second penalty for pit-lane speeding to take sixth. Leclerc wound up seventh, ahead of his Ferrari team mate Carlos Sainz.

There were no red flags or Safety Cars needed, although we did see both Alpines exit the race following a series of collisions on the opening lap, leaving the cars of Esteban Ocon and Pierre Gasly with terminal damage.

Click on the video player above to relive the action from Budapest, as Verstappen seals a record-breaking 12th consecutive victory for Red Bull.

# Raikkonen fails to take the start in Malaysia

Oct 01, 2017 12:00am UTC

![MAS RACE](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/Galleries/2017/2017%20FORMULA%20MALAYSIA%20GRAND%20PRIX%20-%20Kuala%20Lumpur/Sunday%20Race/sunpic4.webp)

Ferrari’s nightmare weekend in Sepang continued on Sunday afternoon, as Kimi Raikkonen was wheeled away from his front-row grid slot and back to the team’s garage just before the start of the 2017 Formula 1 Petronas Malaysia Grand Prix.

With team mate Sebastian Vettel last on the grid after technical problems stopped the German setting a qualifying time on Saturday, Raikkonen was Ferrari’s best hope of a strong race result. However, it was clear that the Finn had problems as he drove to the grid, telling his crew he had no battery charge.

Once on the grid, mechanics worked frantically on his car, removing the engine cover on the SF70H. It was back on in time, and the team looked to have resolved matters. However, a couple of minutes prior to the formation lap, Raikkonen was hurriedly pushed back to the garage, from which he never emerged.

For the latest from the race, check out our [Live Timing](https://www.formula1.com/en/f1-live.html).
